A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DADP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Matching retained and relocated material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original MuJoCo and Adroit evaluations, representation and utilization ablations, and guidance-scale and context-source experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds extrapolation, nonstationary dynamics, inference-efficiency, and representation-diagnostic experiments.

M1.justification: The context encoder, cross-episode representation learning, representation-biased diffusion prior, composite prediction objective, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V3 clarifies the universal infinite-lag default; one-step DDIM is an evaluation of the existing sampler.

E1.justification: V3 adds parameter domains outside the training support for all four MuJoCo environments and four nonstationary Walker2d friction scenarios. Existing locomotion, manipulation, and Meta-DT tasks remain. Renaming the original IID/OOD settings to Seen/Unseen does not itself add coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains CORRO, Prompt-DT, and Meta-DT, while supplementary comparisons reuse existing diffusion and representation-utilization variants. MetaDiffuser receives expanded discussion but is not directly evaluated in either version.

E3.justification: New protocols include five out-of-support parameter sets per MuJoCo environment, changing friction schedules with 50-step switches, one-step versus five-step DDIM sampling, and normalized within-domain representation standard deviation as a diagnostic metric. The existing main training hyperparameter table is retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds nonstationary robustness, inference-step sensitivity, and direct entanglement diagnostics, and extends representation-quality and utilization analyses to Ant and Hopper. The Meta-DT lag ablation is relocated from v2 Table 3 to v3 Table 6; guidance-scale and context-source analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Benchmark reporting remains mean ± standard deviation across five seeds, with no reported change to run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Table 12 introduces representation variability as an evaluation metric, rather than uncertainty about experimental results.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores remain unchanged after matching IID/OOD to Seen/Unseen. New OOD DADP returns are 3371±257, 2197±173, 1903±64, and 1271±48 for HalfCheetah, Walker2d, Ant, and Hopper respectively. Expanded Table 2 and new Tables 9–12 add substantial findings. Table 11 also shows Better Representation outperforming DADP on both Hopper settings, qualifying the broadly favorable utilization narrative.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, diffusion derivations, and Appendix A toy-case reasoning are retained. Separating diffusion index k from environment time t, standardizing action-space notation, and clarifying covariance do not introduce substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised lagged-context representations, diffusion injection, superior zero-shot adaptation, and the released pipeline. Additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations connecting recent-context encoding to tracking changing dynamics and the biased prior to efficient one-step generation. It also interprets Hopper’s weaker separation and proposes probe accuracy as a dataset-diversity diagnostic. These substantially expand applicability and mechanism discussions, while the original stationary-dynamics limitations paragraph remains.

D1.justification: V3 specifies new OOD parameter intervals, friction schedules, checkpoint controls, and inference budgets; existing architecture details, hyperparameters, and project access remain unchanged. Documentation has a new inconsistency: Appendix C.4 gives Walker2d training friction support as [1.12,2.48], whereas Table 4 retains [1.32,2.28].

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Cheng et al. (2026), Liu et al. (2025c), Niu et al. (2024), and Pace et al. (2025). It expands the distinctions from MetaDiffuser and states why no direct comparison is supplied, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted explanatory and notation edits, adopts Seen/Unseen terminology, adds conference publication text and an Impact Statement, and relocates the Meta-DT ablation into Appendix C. The main narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned from two setting-specific panels into grouped Seen/Unseen/OOD bars. Tables 1 and 2 expand, four new tables present supplementary evidence, and the Meta-DT table moves to the appendix. This substantially expands the empirical displays, while most other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 labels held-out domains within the training factor space as OOD. V3 corrects this distinction and supplies actual extrapolation tests, addressing an important gap in the central generalization evidence. Direct representation diagnostics and broader ablations also strengthen mechanistic support. These substantial gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including conflicting Walker2d training ranges and Table 10’s stated 85.8% decrease for 3722 to 158, which actually implies approximately 95.8%.
